lessons.title: Ending blends
lessons.rule: In an ending blend, you can hear both consonant sounds. In pump, listen for m and p at the end.

lessons.title: Double ll and ck
lessons.rule: After a short vowel, many words end in ll or ck. The two letters represent one sound: ll in still and ck in truck.

lessons.title: Digraphs: sh, ch, th
lessons.rule: A digraph is two letters working together for one sound. Listen to sh in ship, ch in chip, and th in thin. The th in this has a different sound from th in thin.

lessons.title: Silent E (magic E)
lessons.rule: A silent e at the end often makes the earlier vowel say its name. Fin becomes fine. This is a useful pattern, but some words, like come, work differently.

questions.prompt: Add silent e to hat. Write the new word.
Add silent e to pin. Write the new word.
Add silent e to cap. Write the new word.
Add silent e to hop. Write the new word.
Add silent e to fin. Write the new word.

lessons.title: Bossy R
lessons.rule: An r after a vowel can change its sound. Listen to ar in yarn, ir in dirt, and ur in hurt. Fire has the ire pattern; its pronunciation can vary by accent.

lessons.title: Vowel teams
lessons.rule: Letters can work together to spell a vowel sound. The same team can have different sounds: compare oo in moon and book. Listen to the whole word rather than guessing from one rule.

lessons.title: Plurals with S
lessons.rule: Add s to many words to show more than one. The ending can sound like s or z. For bunny, change y to ies to make bunnies.

questions.prompt: Write the word for more than one star.
Write the word for more than one wing.
Write the word for more than one step.
Write the word for more than one claw.
Write the word for more than one cat.
Write the word for more than one dog.
Write the word for more than one bunny.

lessons.title: Two-syllable words
lessons.rule: Clap the beats in a word. Each syllable has a vowel sound. Winter has two beats: win · ter. Apple also has two: ap · ple.

questions.prompt: Clap the beats in "winter". How many syllables?

lessons.title: Tricky words
lessons.rule: Some words have a part you need to learn by heart. Say the word, notice the tricky part, then cover it and spell it. Compare come with some, and good with wood.
